Keel Infrastructure.why: Former Bitcoin miner now developing HPC / AI data-center campuses on secured power (Panther Creek PA 350 MW, Sharon PA, Moses Lake WA, Sherbrooke QC) for lease to hyperscalers, AI companies and GPU clouds with 2027 ready-for-service dates; AI compute demand is its sole growth driver.
Keel Infrastructure.evidence: Keel Infrastructure Q2 FY2026 call (08-10-2026), CEO Ben Gagnon: 'Today, we have multiple potential customers negotiating across multiple sites simultaneously ... Hyperscalers, leading AI companies, GPU clouds, and large enterprise' and Panther Creek '350 MW of secured utility capacity with PPL ... our earliest RFS date continues to be 2027.'

players.product: HPC / AI data-center campuses on secured power for lease (Panther Creek PA 350 MW, Sharon PA, Moses Lake WA 18 MW, Sherbrooke QC 96 MW; RFS 2027) - converted from Bitcoin mining

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: second quarter 2026 revenue was $30 million versus $61 million a year earlier, reflecting lower Bitcoin prices and the shutdown of the Moses Lake mining operations. Operating loss was $141 million including $63 million of accelerated depreciation on mining rig shutdowns at Panther Creek and Scrubgrass; adjusted EBITDA was negative $24 million. Total liquidity was $819 million as of August 7th; cash SG&A is tracking $100 million for the year. All U.S. Bitcoin mining has been decommissioned and the remaining 1,861 Bitcoin are to be liquidated in 2026.

CEO: Moses Lake (18 MW; the extra 10 MW option was given up) should be the first site fully permitted, online and generating HPC revenue, as Keel's first fully commissioned and energized data center in 2027 (delayed maybe a couple of months versus original guidance). The first Vertiv modules and long lead items have arrived on site and every piece of critical long lead equipment is secured; leases there may be modified gross rather than triple net, with interest from AI companies, GPU clouds and enterprises.
quarterly_data.figure: Moses Lake 18 MW, first energized data center in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Panther Creek has 350 MW of secured utility capacity with PPL and potential expansion to 500 MW or more; zoning and conditional land development approval were secured, but final environmental permits are taking a few months longer than anticipated, without changing the ESA power delivery schedule or economics. Panther Creek and Sharon both target end of year 2027 ready for service; Keel is looking at compressing the first data center into one 110 MW phase. Sharon has full zoning, land development approval and transformers delivered.
quarterly_data.figure: Panther Creek 350 MW (expandable to 500 MW+); Panther Creek and Sharon RFS end of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: multiple potential customers - hyperscalers, leading AI companies, GPU clouds and large enterprise - are negotiating across all three priority sites, interest far exceeds the capacity Keel has to lease, and multiple tenants want all three sites; no lease is signed yet and Keel will not sign prematurely. Near-term power is scarce and there is still very little 2027 power available in the market.

CEO: Keel is increasingly confident of converting expansion capacity from its 2 GW Pennsylvania pipeline into more signed ESAs through 2030 (update as early as December or January). Sherbrooke has all local approvals, with only provincial approval outstanding, to consolidate three Bitcoin power purchase agreements into a single 96 MW HPC and AI power purchase agreement. Scrubgrass (1 GW+ campus) is in the energy application stage: a load study for 750 MW and a pipeline for 550 MW of on-site CCGT generation.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 GW PA expansion pipeline; Sherbrooke 96 MW PPA pending; Scrubgrass load study 750 MW
